newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica shares seen up on Portugal link.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica shares seen up on Portugal link.

text.p: Shares in Telefonica were higher in line with the market on Tuesday after Portugal Telecom confirmed a share swap with the Spanish operator.
Analysts said the stock may not necessarily outstrip the indices until concrete details of any international partnerships are made official.
Portugal Telecom declined to specify the share swap terms.
At 0935 GMT, Telefonica was up 30 pesetas, 0.87 percent, to 3,465 while the Ibex-35 blue chip index added 0.91 percent to 5,502.81.
The Portuguese agreement will foster the Spanish operator's entry into the lucrative Brasilian market, analysts said.

"Brasil has the largest population in South America but at the same time its (telephone) penetration rate is one of the lowest. It has enormous potential," said Javier Borrachero, analyst at Central Hispano Bolsa.
"I don't think this is in the share price," he added.
An analyst at a Spanish bank said the market was also awaiting details of a U.S. alliance, with most expecting Telefonica to announce a deal with MCI Communications Corp shortly.
"I think it has to be made clear how the set-up in Europe is completed if Telefonica does indeed link up with MCI," he added.
He agreed the Portugal Telecom deal was good news for Telefonica but it was still early to quantify the size of the business there.

"Brasil has very substantial potential. A deal with Portugal Telecom has special interest for Telefonica in that (the former) has an alliance with (partly-privatised state operator) Telebras. But that's hard to put a figure on."
